tasks.short: Survey the power system and correct problems

steps.what: Study the map for open power points
Walk the field survey and record each reading
Build the fault list from survey rows
Decide the power problem and the correction
Apply the signed correction on the system

tasks.design: Maps and a one-line sit on a {BI} view keyed by point id. The electrical engineer walks the site and records point id, reading, and whether it is a fault on a {WORKFLOW} form. A {DOCS} fault list is built only from those rows. A point with no reading stays open. The engineer decides the cause and applies the correction. A model does not choose the correction on the live system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings sat in a notebook, and the map did not show which points had been visited, so the fault list was retyped later.
tasks.enabler_now: A form can store a point id and a reading, and a map view can show which points are still blank.
tasks.still_hard: The cause of a power problem is a judgement on site, and a live correction can be unsafe.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer decides the cause and whether a live correction is safe to make.

ambition.what: Repeat the survey of a corrected point, not only on the yearly round

tasks.altitude: The walk and the correction stay on site. The map shows blank points, and the fault list no longer waits to be retyped. The engineer can refuse a correction that was not signed.

reach.task: Finish a correction the engineer signed and did not complete on site
reach.learn: Which point ids are signed and which points have no reading

evidence.claim: A power-system survey is a site walk plus a map. The walk and the correction stay with the engineer. The fault list can be filled from the readings they recorded.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say a safety component in electricity can be high-risk AI. The cause and the correction are not chosen by a model.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task ends when a signed correction has been applied or explicitly stopped. A project to rebuild the feeder is later.
Input contract: point id, reading, unit, fault yes or no, map sheet id. Producer is the engineer on site. A point with no reading stays open and is not given a guessed value.
The map view uses the existing diagram export. Native views are configured before custom code.
The site walk and the live correction stay with the person. The high in-person prior is time on site, so those steps stay in person rather than becoming a meeting.
unknowns: Whether a second person is required for live electrical work.
Who may sign a correction when the engineer is off site.
research_questions: What share of map points has no reading after a survey?
How often is the first correction reversed?

already_counted.description: Engineer still checks the map for points the export missed
The field survey stays with the engineer
Cause and correction choice stay with the engineer
Live correction work stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Update the point list when a feeder is altered

approvals.approved_version: correction decision for this survey and point

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes readings stay in a notebook, so the list is still typed by hand and only the map view is new. The high case assumes the list is built from the form, but the walk, the cause, and the correction stay manual. A rebuild project is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Design lighting that uses less electric energy

steps.what: Mark lighting zones and the emergency level
Copy the daylight factor for each lighting zone

loop.output: a daylight factor per zone that exists in the log
loop.check: The factor equals the value printed for that zone id
loop.stop: If the log has no zone id, leave the factor blank and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Log layouts differ by study, so a fixed cell can copy the wrong room

steps.what: Calculate ordinary lighting counts from signed zones
Review natural lighting use with the space user
Sign the lighting design that cuts energy use

tasks.design: The electrical engineer marks each zone in {DOCS}: area, occupied hours, daylight yes or no, and the emergency level. A {SPREADSHEET} calculates an ordinary lighting count only from the wattage the engineer selected and a daylight factor copied from a simulation log. If the log has no factor, the count stays blank. The formula cannot write the emergency column. The meeting with the space user stays a meeting. One signed version is filed. This design is not an energy information report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Zone areas, daylight notes, and lamp counts lived in separate sheets, so a count could not show which daylight figure it used.
tasks.enabler_now: A zone list can carry an area and an emergency level, and a daylight log can carry a zone id that a factor must match.
tasks.still_hard: The allowance, the hours of use, and the emergency level are judgements. A daylight run can be the wrong room.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer sets the ordinary allowance and the emergency level, and can reject a daylight factor from the wrong zone.

ambition.what: Re-sign the count when the hours of use change, not only when the lamps are replaced

tasks.altitude: Ordinary counts take less arithmetic. Zone choices, the user meeting, and the emergency level stay. The engineer can refuse a count that used a blank daylight factor.

reach.task: Draw the lighting layout from the signed zone list
reach.learn: Which zones are signed and which ordinary counts were left blank

evidence.claim: A lighting scheme that uses daylight is a zone list, a calculation, and a talk with the people who use the space. The allowance and the emergency level are the engineer's.
Digest [S11] says an executable simulation call is not a correct result, so a daylight factor is copied only when it matches the log for that zone.
Digest [S12] and [S13] say a safety component in electricity can be high-risk AI. The calculation must not propose or reduce the emergency light level.

assumptions: Focal role is the electrical engineer. The task ends at a signed lighting version. Installation is a later task.

Input contract: zone id, area, occupied hours, daylight yes or no, ordinary wattage, emergency level, simulation run id. Producer of the levels is the engineer. Producer of the factor is the daylight log. A missing factor leaves the ordinary count blank.
The count is a spreadsheet formula. Native formulas are used before custom code. The formula has no write into the emergency column.
This is a design, not an energy information report. No consumption threshold is a formula in this sheet.
The meeting with the space user stays with the person.
unknowns: Whether a later energy information duty will use this design, and any site threshold, which must be confirmed and is not applied here.
Who sets the emergency level, the engineer or a safety adviser.
Which daylight study is the run of record.
research_questions: What share of zones has no daylight result in the log?
How often does the user meeting change the hours or the emergency level?

already_counted.description: Zone and emergency choices stay with the engineer
Engineer checks daylight factors against the log
User meeting stays with the engineer
Signature time stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Update wattage rows when a lamp type is added to the catalogue

approvals.approved_version: zone list with emergency levels for this scheme
lighting version signed for this scheme

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes there is no usable daylight log, so counts stay manual and the engineer still builds the sheet. The high case assumes ordinary counts calculate, but zone choices, the user meeting, the emergency level, and the signature stay. Installation and any statutory energy filing are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Surveys stay on site and lighting choices stay with the electrical engineer. What moves is the fault list and the ordinary lamp count.
reach: The electrical technician receives a signed fault list from the survey, not a notebook page.
The engineering drafter draws only the lighting version the engineer signed.
skills_to_grow: Record a survey reading as a point id and a value, and leave a point blank rather than guess.
Keep the emergency light level as a signed figure the ordinary count cannot change.
role.ambitious_version: Each power survey ends with a signed fault list, and each low-energy lighting scheme names the daylight assumption that was used.
